requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: mtr and its dependencies were fetched into /srv/localrepo/x86_64 and an APKINDEX.tar.gz was built there (cmd-f6e6c0fe653a456b). After discovering busybox lacks an httpd applet (cmd-3e9c3c14e1d141ed), darkhttpd was installed and started as a daemon bound to the node's own IP on port 8080 serving that directory, with a verified HTTP 200 response to the index file (cmd-ee9103e7969b4197).

requirements.requirement: Usual remote repositories unreachable while the install is performed
requirements.summary: dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org was blackholed via /etc/hosts and curl to the remote index timed out (http_code=000) immediately before the install was performed, directly demonstrating the disruption in effect at install time.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while remote is unreachable
requirements.summary: With /etc/apk/repositories pointed exclusively at http://$NODE_IP:8080 and the remote blackholed, apk update/add --allow-untrusted succeeded and installed mtr (plus jansson dependency); apk info -e mtr and mtr --version confirmed the working install.

requirements.requirement: Restore normal repository/network configuration after the demonstration
requirements.summary: /etc/apk/repositories and /etc/hosts were restored from backups, remote reachability was reconfirmed (http_code=200), and mtr remained installed. Post-restart evidence further confirms clean config with no leftover hosts blackhole entry.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 3587c063-...-9bf7-ee49f6989bd8, healthy mtr, and local repo file md5 (cmd-c1753fffc3224277). A delayed reboot was issued and acknowledged before disconnect (cmd-0b9f465fdc184f6c), followed by observed connection loss across several polls (cmd-e863091c664044a2 through cmd-3c17467833f245c3) and a new boot_id b7634457-2ee2-472f-9896-53e94b30cbe5 on reconnection (cmd-8aa5f031965e46fd). Post-restart recovery of the package, unchanged local repo file md5, restored apk config, and remote reachability was confirmed (cmd-aaa399363f3040e1). This is corroborated by the fixed global before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots, which show the identical boot_id transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly demonstrated: a local-storage apk repository was built and served over HTTP via darkhttpd, the usual remote CDN was made unreachable via a hosts blackhole and confirmed unreachable at install time, mtr was successfully installed from the local repo under that condition, and normal configuration was restored afterward. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also fully satisfied with a coherent pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery of the package, local repo data, and network config, cross-checked against the fixed global boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is good but not perfect: a few bounded, failed busybox-httpd troubleshooting attempts and an unstopped darkhttpd daemon (cleared only incidentally by the reboot) and unconfirmed removal of .bak files are minor blemishes.
limitations: No direct evidence that /etc/apk/repositories.bak and /etc/hosts.bak backup files were removed after use.
darkhttpd was not explicitly stopped during the restore step; its termination is inferred only from the absence of a port 8080 listener in the after_executor snapshot, not from a direct stop command.
prepare phase was disabled (alias of before_prepare), so preparation-specific comparison offers no additional signal beyond the before/after_executor comparison.

operational_hygiene.summary: Three troubleshooting attempts to serve the repo via busybox httpd (cmd-00666fec348d4813, cmd-d838b133ae53426f, cmd-3e9c3c14e1d141ed) each issued pkill and attempted to spawn a listener before discovering busybox lacks an httpd applet; these were bounded, low-risk, self-contained failed experiments that left no residue (no busybox httpd process ever started) and were superseded by the working darkhttpd approach, so they are noted but only mildly penalized. The darkhttpd daemon and its listening socket on port 8080 were left running unstopped from the demonstration through to the reboot (cmd-ee9103e7969b4197 onward) rather than being explicitly stopped during the restore step (cmd-53ca44961a9c4931); this was incidentally cleared by the subsequent reboot and did not persist afterward, per the after_executor listening-sockets snapshot which shows only sshd/dhcpcd and no port 8080 listener. Backup files /etc/apk/repositories.bak and /etc/hosts.bak created during the demo are not confirmed removed in any captured evidence, a minor residue risk. No damaged package state, unsafe exposure, or destructive mutations were observed; the added /tmp/reboot.log is an expected artifact of the mandatory restart step.
